preamble: Fronting of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] all the way to the alveolar sibilant [z] before front vowels. In Modern Greek dialects velar fronting usually stops at palatal [ʝ] (the standard allophone) or palato-alveolar [ʒ]; full alveolar [z] from /ɣ/ is a rare outcome, recorded on Kea and in traces on Sikinos and Folegandros, and in some Dodecanese varieties (Kalymnos, Nisyros, Patmos).

languageExamples.language: Modern Greek (Kea, Kalymnos, Nisyros, Patmos dialects)

examples.note: Older Kea speech showed [ɣ] > [z] fronting without the matching change [k] > [s] (Kollia 1933); in the Dodecanese, fronting of [ɣ] to [z] or [ʑ] is attested on Kalymnos, Nisyros and Patmos. Manolessou & Pantelidis classify these by synchronic outcome and do not reconstruct intermediate stages.

sources: Manolessou, I., & Pantelidis, N. (2012). Velar fronting in Modern Greek dialects. Modern Greek Dialects and Linguistic Theory 5(1), 272–286. https://pasithee.library.upatras.gr/mgdlt/article/view/2599
